name: Switzerland
genZNote: Switzerland has stayed neutral through both World Wars while still hosting the Red Cross, dozens of UN agencies, and most global diplomacy in Geneva — proof that 'neutral' doesn't mean 'irrelevant,' it means 'everyone trusts you enough to meet there.'

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A landlocked country in Central Europe, bordered by Germany, France, Italy, Austria, and Liechtenstein, dominated by the Alps mountain range.
Home to numerous glacial lakes (Geneva, Lucerne, Zurich) and is a major source of several major European rivers, including the Rhine and Rhône.
Divided into 26 cantons, many with strong local autonomy reflecting the country's linguistic and cultural diversity.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Has four official languages — German, French, Italian, and Romansh — reflecting its position at the crossroads of major European cultures.
Known for a strong direct democracy tradition, with frequent national referendums on major policy issues.
Renowned globally for precision watchmaking, chocolate, and a culture of quality craftsmanship.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal republic with a unique collective executive: a seven-member Federal Council governs collegially, with the presidency rotating annually among its members.
Maintains a long-standing policy of armed neutrality, having not participated in an international war for over two centuries.
Known for extensive direct democracy, where citizens can call binding referendums on a wide range of national and cantonal policy questions.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Home to CERN, the world's largest particle physics laboratory, where the Higgs boson was confirmed and the World Wide Web was invented.
A global pharmaceutical powerhouse, home to Novartis and Roche, two of the world's largest pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies.
Consistently ranks among the world's most innovative countries, with strong investment in research and development relative to GDP.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Not a European Union or NATO member, maintaining its historic policy of neutrality, though closely integrated with the EU through bilateral agreements.
Hosts the European headquarters of the United Nations in Geneva, along with the International Committee of the Red Cross and numerous other international organisations.
A global centre for international diplomacy, arbitration, and banking given its neutral status and stability.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Switzerland maintain long-standing friendly relations, with Switzerland being a source of significant investment and advanced pharmaceutical and precision manufacturing technology.
Both countries cooperate through the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), with a landmark EFTA-India trade agreement signed in 2024 covering investment and trade expansion.
Switzerland has historically been a significant location for Indian banking and financial matters, a subject of periodic bilateral discussion on financial transparency.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A wealthy, highly specialised economy strong in pharmaceuticals, precision instruments, banking/finance, and luxury watchmaking.
Home to major global companies including Nestlé, Novartis, Roche, and UBS.
A global financial centre known for banking, insurance, and wealth management services.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Long-standing political neutrality and hosting major international diplomatic institutions in Geneva.
World-class precision watchmaking and chocolate.
CERN and major global pharmaceutical companies (Novartis, Roche).
Extensive direct democracy through frequent national referendums.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Switzerland is a neutral, federal, direct-democratic republic in the Alps, home to CERN and major global diplomatic institutions in Geneva, though not an EU or NATO member.
keyFacts: Federal republic with a rotating seven-member collective executive (Federal Council).
Four official languages: German, French, Italian, Romansh.
Hosts CERN and the UN's European headquarters in Geneva; historically neutral, not in EU or NATO.
commonConfusion: Switzerland is NOT a member of the European Union or NATO, despite being geographically central to Europe — it maintains a historic policy of armed neutrality.

highYieldFacts: Switzerland: federal republic, rotating Federal Council presidency, capital Bern.
Not an EU or NATO member; maintains armed neutrality; hosts UN Geneva HQ and CERN.
India-Switzerland: EFTA-India trade agreement signed 2024; strong pharma/precision-manufacturing ties.
commonTraps: Assuming Switzerland is an EU member because it's in Europe — it is not, and uses its own currency (Swiss Franc).
Confusing Switzerland's rotating collective presidency with a single powerful head of state.
mustRemember: Switzerland: neutral federal republic, CERN/Geneva diplomacy hub, EFTA-India trade deal (2024), major pharma partner.
